I've been a neurogastroenterologist for 21 years. And if you've been told that magnesium is the "natural" alternative to Miralax for the constipation your GLP-1 has been giving you, and you're now taking 800, 1,000, 1,200mg every night and still getting worse, I'm about to tell you exactly what most of my profession won't.

Magnesium citrate is not a supplement.

It is a laxative.

The same FDA category as Miralax. The same osmotic mechanism. The same dependency curve.

The only difference is the aisle it sits in.

I am writing this because the wellness industry has built a multi-billion dollar business out of repackaging an osmotic laxative as a calming mineral, and most of my own profession has either gone along with it or stayed quiet about it.

I am not going to stay quiet anymore.

Magnesium citrate, magnesium oxide, magnesium hydroxide, every salt of magnesium that has ever been recommended to a woman on a GLP-1 for constipation, works the exact same way. It pulls water osmotically into the colon, which forces a bowel movement.

That is precisely what Miralax does.

That is precisely what Milk of Magnesia does.

Your bottle of Miralax sits in the laxative aisle. Your bottle of Milk of Magnesia sits in the laxative aisle. Your bottle of magnesium citrate sits in the supplement aisle.

The chemistry is the same. The aisle is not.

That is the entire trick.

Milk of Magnesia is magnesium hydroxide. It has been sold as a laxative in this country since 1873. It carries an FDA-required warning on the label. It tells you not to use it for more than 7 days. It tells you to call a doctor if you have to.

Nobody calls Milk of Magnesia a wellness supplement.

Now take that same magnesium ion. Bind it to citrate instead of hydroxide. Print "calm support" on the label. Put a picture of a leaf on the bottle. Move it 4 aisles over.

We have collectively agreed to pretend it is a different product.

It is not a different product.

It is a laxative with better marketing.

The active ion that pulls water into your colon is the same ion that pulls water into your colon out of the Milk of Magnesia bottle that your grandmother used to keep behind the toilet and was embarrassed about.

Same drug. Different bottle.

The reason this happened is not complicated.

The supplement aisle has higher margins. Supplements do not require FDA premarket review. Supplements do not carry the laxative warning. Supplements do not carry the 7-day limit. Supplements do not have to tell you what category of drug they actually are.

A bottle of magnesium citrate in the supplement aisle costs 4 times what the same dose of Milk of Magnesia costs in the laxative aisle, and the woman buying it walks out of the store thinking she has bought a vitamin.

That is the business model.

It is working on women on GLP-1 medications most of all, because those are the women in this country right now who are the most desperate for something that sounds gentle and does not sound like a laxative.

I want to tell you why none of this was ever going to work, regardless of which aisle you bought it from.

GLP-1 medications work in 2 places. Not 1.

The appetite suppression, the part that actually makes you eat less, happens in your brain. That is the engine of your weight loss. That is why the pounds are coming off. That is the part of the medication you do not want to undo.

But the medication does a second thing.

It takes your stomach from normal to nearly frozen.

Food that should leave the stomach in 4 hours sits there for 10. 12. Sometimes 14.

And while it sits there, bacteria ferment it.

That fermentation is where every symptom you have been suffering through comes from.

The gas. The bloating. The constipation. The sulfur burps. The pressure under your ribs by 4pm. The brick that will not pass.

Every single one of those symptoms originates in your stomach.

Not your colon.

This is the part of the letter where I want you to stop and read slowly.

Magnesium works on your colon.

Miralax works on your colon. Dulcolax works on your colon. Senna works on your colon. Colace works on your colon. Fiber works on your colon. Every laxative in every aisle in every drugstore in this country works on your colon.

All of them work 6 feet downstream from where the actual problem is.

Your medication slowed your stomach. The wellness industry sold you a colon laxative dressed up as a vitamin.

You have been hydrating an empty pipe.

The food is still trapped 6 feet upstream.

That is why the dose you started with stopped working. That is why you doubled it. That is why you doubled it again. That is the dependency curve every laxative produces, regardless of what aisle it is sold in.

And every week you keep taking it, your body forgets a little more how to move on its own.

I watched this happen to my own mother.

She took daily magnesium for 22 years on the advice of a primary care doctor who told her it was just a vitamin. Her bowels physically forgot how to move. Her world shrank to 4 walls.

The last Christmas I drove down to see her, she sat at her kitchen table and would not eat the meal she had cooked.

She said, "I'm sorry. If I eat I won't go for 8 days. I have learned to just not eat."

I watched my own mother decide not to eat Christmas dinner.

I cannot save her. I might be able to save you.

Here is what actually works for a stomach that the medication has nearly frozen.

3 things, working together, on the right organ.

The first is apigenin. A plant compound concentrated in celery. It works on the smooth muscle of the stomach wall, gently helping the contractions start again. Not a laxative. Not a stimulant. Not a dependency.

And critically, it does not override your medication.

The brain part, the appetite suppression, the actual engine of your weight loss, is not touched. Apigenin only works on the stomach side effect. The drug keeps doing its weight-loss job. The food stops fermenting inside you.

The second is chlorophyllin, which binds the sulfur compounds your fermenting stomach bacteria are producing. It neutralizes the bloating and the burps at the source.

The third is a soluble prebiotic fiber in a small targeted dose. Not bulk-forming. Not Metamucil. A different category of fiber that supports the lower gut once the upstream issue is resolved.

The product I send my patients to is called Motilli. Standardized apigenin extract from celery, not powder. Combined with chlorophyllin and the soluble prebiotic. 2 gummies a day.

I started recommending it for 1 reason.

I have watched it work in my own exam room, in too many of my patients, to call it a coincidence.

The women I put on it come back in 6 weeks looking less puffy. Sleeping flat again. Off the magnesium. Off the Miralax. Still losing weight on their pen.

So here is what I am asking you to do tonight.

If you are on a GLP-1 and taking magnesium every night, stop. Call your doctor in the morning and tell them what dose you have been taking, and ask them what the bottle of Milk of Magnesia in their pharmacy says about the same active ion.

Read the back of your magnesium bottle. Look for the words "saline laxative" or "osmotic laxative" in the active ingredient panel. They are there on most of them. Most women have never read them.

If you have been doubling, tripling, quadrupling the dose because the original stopped working, that is not a sign you need more magnesium. That is the dependency curve telling you to get off it.

Motilli runs a 90-day money-back guarantee. They batch-produce because apigenin degrades from light and heat, so the bottles sell out for stretches when more women in the GLP-1 communities find them. If you have a vacation, a holiday, a wedding coming up, I would not wait until next week.

The link is below.
